newsitem.title: USA: NYC Bar Association eyes "pay-to-play" ban plan.
newsitem.headline: NYC Bar Association eyes "pay-to-play" ban plan.

text.p: The Association of the Bar of the City of New York said Tuesday it had placed a proposal to ban "pay-to-play" by municipal bond lawyers on the August meeting agenda of the American Bar Association House of Delegates.
The proposal would prohibit lawyers from securing government finance work, including muni bond work, from governmental entities within two years of making campaign contributions to those entities.
The proposal was on the House of delegates agenda last August, but was withdrawn to provide an opportunity to receive comments from interested ABA entities, the association said in a statement.

A number of those comments have been incorporated, including the maximum allowable contribution -- now set at $1,000 -- by a lawyer to a political party, which may in turn fund candidates who oversee the awarding on bond issues.
The contribution was increased to $1,000 from $250.

"The prevalence of 'pay-to-play' practices within the legal community is of the utmost concern to the City Bar," said Association president Michael A Cardozo. "It is imperative that attorneys monitor their own actions so they are better able to ensure the public of a high standard of integrity."

The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board currently has rules in place to bar bond dealers from engaging in pay-to- play activities to influence selection for bond work and penalize them if the firms do.
